bull_case: Search monetization remains resilient while Cloud backlog converts, AI products expand wallet share, and the 2026 infrastructure buildout normalizes into much higher owner FCF/share. Excluded strategic equity holdings add unmodeled upside.
bear_case: AI search economics require persistently higher compute cost, capex remains structurally near operating cash flow, external financing continues, and regulation weakens distribution or ad monetization.
thesis: At $354.97, Alphabet trades modestly above the locked Base DCF of $335.36 while remaining well below the $543.99 Bull value. The core valuation issue is whether owner FCF/share can recover from the 2026 AI-capex trough; H1 operating cash flow of $84.9B was nearly absorbed by $80.6B of capex. Cloud growth/backlog make recovery plausible, but current price already requires roughly Base execution and the model remains sensitive to capex normalization.

evidence.claim: H1 2026 operating cash flow was $84.859B while purchases of property and equipment were $80.598B, showing unusually compressed owner cash flow during the AI infrastructure buildout.
Q2 2026 revenue was $119.796B, up 24% YoY, and Google Cloud revenue growth was 82% YoY.
Revenue backlog reached about $519.5B in Q2 2026, with the large majority tied to Google Cloud and just over half expected to be recognized over the next 24 months.
Alphabet raised large amounts of equity/preferred capital in June 2026 and completed an additional $25B senior-note offering in August, consistent with a step-up in AI infrastructure financing.

Using the locked 9% required return, 15x/20x/25x terminal multiples and $4.411 net cash/share, the submitted 10-year owner-FCF/share paths imply about $95.57 Bear, $335.36 Base and $543.99 Bull value; $354.97 price/Base is 1.0585x.
evidence.source: Harness locked owner-FCF/share DCF using frozen 2026-09-21 GOOGL inputs

counterevidence: The DCF excludes substantial strategic equity holdings from conservative net cash, potentially understating asset value.
Cloud backlog above $500B provides unusually strong contracted-demand visibility, although backlog is not equivalent to profit or free cash flow.
A meaningful portion of current capex is likely growth investment; if utilization and AI monetization scale, present FCF compression can reverse sharply.
Search, YouTube, Cloud, subscriptions and Other Bets create several independent value pools rather than a single AI outcome.
unknowns: Normalized maintenance versus growth capex after the current AI infrastructure buildout.
Incremental return on 2025-2027 AI infrastructure investment.
Long-run Search margin after AI inference costs and changing answer formats.
Economic value realizable from SpaceX and other strategic equity holdings.
falsifiers: Capex remains near or above operating cash flow for several years without corresponding acceleration in Cloud/Search owner earnings.
Cloud backlog converts at materially lower margins or utilization than assumed while financing continues.
Regulatory remedies structurally impair Search distribution or ad monetization enough that normalized owner FCF/share cannot approach the Base path.
